sa_market_summary: The Golf 7 (2013-2020) and Golf 7.5 facelift (2018-2022) are among the most sought-after used hatchbacks in South Africa. Excellent build quality relative to competitors and strong brand prestige. GTI models hold value exceptionally well. Widely available and well-supported by VW dealers and independent specialists nationwide. A safe, intelligent purchase for the used car buyer who wants European refinement without supercar running costs.

known_faults.description: The DQ200 7-speed dry-clutch DSG is the most common fault on SA Golf 7s. Symptoms include shuddering, hesitation, and occasional loss of drive. Mechatronic unit replacement is expensive. SA's city traffic accelerates DSG wear.
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Insist on a DSG fluid service history (every 40,000km at minimum). Test drive in traffic for shudder. Request VAG-COM scan for DSG fault codes. Consider models with the DQ250 wet-clutch DSG (GTI, GTD) which is more durable.
known_faults.source: VW SA technical bulletins, MyBroadband Golf 7 thread, SA specialist workshops

known_faults.fault: Carbon buildup on intake valves (1.4 TSI)
known_faults.description: Direct injection 1.4 TSI engines accumulate carbon deposits on intake valves. Causes rough idle, reduced power, and increased fuel consumption.
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Request walnut blasting service record. A well-maintained car should have this done by 80,000km.
known_faults.source: SA VW specialist reports, VW owners forum

known_faults.description: Front and rear window regulators fail intermittently. The plastic clips and cable mechanisms are the weak point. Common across all Golf 7 variants.
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Test every window up and down before purchase. Check for slow or jerky operation.
known_faults.source: VW dealer service records, SA owner reports

known_faults.description: The EA888 Gen 3 engine used in the GTI and R is known for timing chain stretch at higher mileage, particularly if oil changes were delayed. Engine rattle on cold start is the primary symptom.
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Listen for cold start chain rattle. Request full service history with proof of regular oil changes (every 10,000-15,000km max with correct 5W-30 oil). Budget for chain inspection on any example above 100,000km.
known_faults.source: Volkswagen technical service bulletins, GTI enthusiast community

known_faults.description: Turbos fail on high-mileage examples, especially on cars where oil service intervals were stretched or incorrect oil was used. Modified GTIs with a Stage 1 tune are higher risk.
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Check exhaust for blue smoke under acceleration. Listen for turbo whine or whistle. Ask if the car has been mapped or tuned.
known_faults.source: SA performance workshop reports, MyBroadband Golf GTI thread

what_to_inspect_before_buying: Full VAG-COM diagnostic scan — non-negotiable on any Golf 7
DSG service history — reject any car without documented DSG fluid changes
Check for timing chain noise on cold start (GTI and R models)
Test all windows, sunroof, and interior electronics
Check for any mapping or performance modifications (affects insurance and warranty)
Inspect for water ingress in the boot through the rear light seals
Check brake disc and pad thickness — performance variants wear brakes faster
Confirm no outstanding safety or emission recalls via VW SA recall database
owner_sentiment: Highly positive overall. Golf 7 GTI owners are passionate about the car and most report excellent long-term reliability if serviced correctly. Standard 1.4 TSI owners report the DSG as the main concern. Running costs are moderate — not cheap, but predictable. Strong community support via MyBroadband and VW clubs.
